small_guidance:
- The clamp/div epilogue is already memory-bound and tiny relative to ConvTranspose3d; further tuning of BLOCK_SIZE/num_warps will not move the needle. If staying small, at least fuse the epilogue in-place (write back into the conv output buffer) to avoid the extra allocation and full read+write pass over ~28M elements.
- Ensure inputs/weights are in channels_last_3d memory format before the conv to let cuDNN pick faster kernels, and keep cudnn.benchmark=True warmup-aware.
- Consider folding the divisor into the conv weight/bias (weight/divisor, bias/divisor) at eval time so the epilogue only does clamp(x, min_value/divisor)·1 — one less multiply per element.
large_guidance:
- ConvTranspose3d dominates runtime (fast_p≈0.86 with the epilogue already trivial). Replace it with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile), iterating over IC and (kd,kh,kw), accumulating input × weight outer products into the output grid with stride/padding index math. Fuse clamp and ×(1/divisor) into the epilogue of this kernel so no second pass over the output is needed.
- Alternative design: implement as a gather-style GEMM where each output voxel (n, oc, od, oh, ow) loops over the (kd,kh,kw) taps that land on it — for stride=2,pad=1,k=3 only a small subset of taps contribute per output voxel (1–8), so a direct gather kernel with precomputed valid-tap masks may beat im2col. Use channels_last layout so IC is the contiguous GEMM-K axis.
- Use triton.autotune over BLOCK_OC ∈ {32,64,128}, BLOCK_SPATIAL ∈ {32,64,128}, num_warps ∈ {4,8}, num_stages ∈ {2,3,4}, keyed on (OC, D*H*W). Bake stride/padding/kernel_size as tl.constexpr so the inner index math is fully unrolled.
